nz-0ffI.title: Plate: white with black text
nz-0ffI.summary: White plates with black text that look mostly white through the blur. Custom plates can make the sides look blue or black, and help tell it from some Australian states.

nz-2F6z.title: Route numbers: two-digit highways, north to south
nz-2F6z.summary: Two-digit state highway numbers increase from north to south. The few single-digit highways cross large parts of the country. Bollards sometimes carry highway numbers.

nz-2dwa.title: Pole: white paint on the middle of the crossbar
nz-2dwa.summary: Some concrete poles have white paint on the middle of their wooden crossbars, in eastern Waikato and one river city, and in parts of several nearby North Island regions.

nz-2qIN.title: Landscape: teal glacial lakes
nz-2qIN.summary: The mountains around the adventure-sports town have many glacial lakes with teal colour and clear water.

nz-3BCb.title: Pole: long cylindrical silver possum guard
nz-3BCb.summary: Many poles in the far south have a long cylindrical silver possum guard. Rarely also in western Otago.

nz-3LkP.title: Landscape: cut-off volcano top like a frog
nz-3LkP.summary: A volcano with a flat-looking top that resembles a frog, with two big 'eyes' on either side.

nz-3zI5.title: Marker: bridge markers, yellow river name
nz-3zI5.summary: Most paved roads have bridge markers. On a state highway the number is in a red crest on a white marker, with the river or bridge name on a yellow marker. Some mark tiny streams or culverts.

nz-4EJh.title: Google car: white and blue front
nz-4EJh.summary: A car with a white and blue front, mostly on the North Island. Occasionally in Canterbury and Marlborough on the South Island.

nz-5Uh0.title: Farming: corn, North Island only
nz-5Uh0.summary: Corn is almost only found on the North Island.

nz-6R0C.title: Street signs: town-specific designs, north
nz-6R0C.summary: Many towns and cities in the north have their own street sign designs, shown in the graphic.

nz-6R9A.title: Landscape: two mountains in flat land
nz-6R9A.summary: A long range with two small bumps to the west, and a volcanic cone to the south, standing up from otherwise flat land.

nz-8lMO.title: Signs: farm sign first digit follows region
nz-8lMO.summary: The first digit of dairy-company farm signs follows the regional pattern on the map.

nz-9ga3.title: Landscape: drier, rolling hills in the north
nz-9ga3.summary: In the north of the North Island: drier climate and rolling hills, especially hilly in the far north. This type of landscape also appears elsewhere on the North Island.

nz-Acdh.title: Landscape: wide green valley, SW to NE
nz-Acdh.summary: Two neighbouring cities sit in a wide green valley running south-west to north-east.

nz-AkRe.title: Landscape: forested mountains rising from water
nz-AkRe.summary: Densely forested mountains rising straight out of the water in the far north of the South Island, almost entirely Gen 4.

nz-BatA.title: Coverage: damaged roads, empty house plots
nz-BatA.summary: After a big 2011 earthquake, 2012 coverage in one South Island city shows bad roads and driveways cut off by water, dirt or mud. Newer coverage shows suburbs with almost no houses, where old driveways remain.

nz-C0Pf.title: City: very hilly capital
nz-C0Pf.summary: The capital city is easy to recognise by how hilly it is.

nz-C3QC.title: Landscape: big snowy mountain range
nz-C3QC.summary: A large snowy mountain range runs through most of the South Island. The further south, the sparser the plants on the mountains.

nz-Ce48.title: Chevron: black on yellow with black border
nz-Ce48.summary: Black-on-yellow chevrons with a thin black border. White-on-black ones are very rare. Australia has the same colours but no border.

nz-E7Wd.title: Google car: Gen 2 coverage and gravel, far north
nz-E7Wd.summary: Gen 2 coverage and gravel roads are particularly common in the far north. Not exclusive, so use other clues.

nz-GdlA.title: Google car: blurred white-blue-white pattern
nz-GdlA.summary: A Street View car with a white-blue-white pattern, blurred out, mainly on the South Island or around and north of the biggest city.

nz-IFOm.title: Fence: wooden with big gaps
nz-IFOm.summary: Wooden fences with big gaps are most common on the South Island and in Taranaki.

nz-IXZs.title: Landscape: cold, stunted plants, alpine slopes
nz-IXZs.summary: The flatter parts of the far south have a cold climate and sloping alpine hills, with stunted vegetation.

nz-JeNW.title: Road: give-way triangles painted on the road
nz-JeNW.summary: Intersections often have give-way triangles painted on the road. Australia does not use this.

nz-JkFp.title: Coverage: dark volcanic ground, no plants
nz-JkFp.summary: Dark volcanic landscape with a clear lack of vegetation, only on the roads around one ski village on a volcano.

nz-KXiR.title: Coverage: bay full of small boats, Gen 3 only
nz-KXiR.summary: An island with coverage only around one settlement, recognisable by a distinct bay often filled with small boats. Only Gen 3.

nz-KqxA.title: Sign: green direction signs, red crest numbers
nz-KqxA.summary: Green direction signs. On a state highway the number is always in a red crest. Brown signs point to landmarks.

nz-LSKR.title: Fence: short wooden extensions on posts
nz-LSKR.summary: Short pieces of wood attached to a fence post, slightly extending it, are common in Hawke's Bay and occasional in Manawatū-Whanganui and Gisborne.

nz-MNql.title: Bins: council logo on the front
nz-MNql.summary: Several cities have distinctive rubbish bins with the council logo on the front. Lid colour varies within cities. Green lids are rare outside one southern city.

nz-Meh7.title: Pole: concrete with one long indent
nz-Meh7.summary: Most common pole is concrete with one long indent running most of the way up, usually with small silver possum guards. Round wooden poles and holey concrete poles also appear.

nz-Nr89.title: Landscape: temperate rainforest, rugged hills
nz-Nr89.summary: On the South Island's west coast and part of the north-west: temperate rainforest and rugged land, with hundreds of tall hills and dark, compact greenery from heavy rain.

nz-NrdM.title: Pole: square concrete, no indent
nz-NrdM.summary: Square concrete poles without the usual indent are most common in the far south, but also in a few other regions.

nz-NyjD.title: Pole: holey concrete poles
nz-NyjD.summary: Holey poles are most common in the far south and around the biggest city.

nz-P4oS.title: Bollard: green stripe
nz-P4oS.summary: A normal bollard but with a green stripe, common in southern Canterbury and a few spots in eastern Southland.

nz-PPp1.title: Plants: very tall hedges
nz-PPp1.summary: Very tall hedges, mainly around one North Island port city. Slightly lower but still tall hedges appear on the South Island plains.

nz-Pwwm.title: Street signs: town-specific designs, south
nz-Pwwm.summary: Many towns and cities in the south have their own street sign designs, shown in the graphic.

nz-RMn3.title: Fence: wooden with tightly packed posts
nz-RMn3.summary: Wooden fences with tightly packed posts are most common on the North Island, the north of the South Island and Banks Peninsula.

nz-RcrP.title: Landscape: dry golden grassy hills
nz-RcrP.summary: A region on the east coast of the North Island has dry, golden grassy hills. In Gen 4 it is sunny with a white car.

nz-SPE9.title: Landscape: rocky peninsula, grassy hills, gorse
nz-SPE9.summary: A rocky peninsula with grassy hills and small patches of trees. Gorse can appear, as it does on the Otago peninsula.

nz-SVyX.title: Plants: cabbage trees, gorse, flax, pine groves
nz-SVyX.summary: A peninsula east of a southern city combines cabbage trees, yellow-flowered gorse, small groves of cone-shaped pines and flax, plus poles with off-centre crossbars.

nz-T8cO.title: Plants: tall hedge and tree rows on flat plains
nz-T8cO.summary: Tall hedges and tree rows are common on a huge flat plain of big fields in the east of the South Island, with mountains in the distance to the west. Even taller hedges appear near one North Island port city.

nz-WY9A.title: Signs: unique bus stop signs in big cities
nz-WY9A.summary: The three biggest cities each have their own unique bus stop signs, shown in the graphic.

nz-Wlc1.title: Pole: orange 'DANGER LIVE WIRES' rectangle
nz-Wlc1.summary: Poles near Timaru often have a tall orange rectangle with the text 'DANGER LIVE WIRES'.

nz-WnqU.title: Pole: long black sticker, 6 digits and a square
nz-WnqU.summary: A long black vertical sticker with 6 digits and a small black square below, on most of the North Island and in the far south. North Island numbers start with 3 or 4, South Island with 8. A similar one without the square is regional, and it can rarely be white.

nz-X2dH.title: Road lines: white outer, yellow double middle
nz-X2dH.summary: White outer lines, with yellow dashed outer lines in built-up areas and none on small roads. Inner lines are a single dashed white or solid double yellow. Australia has no yellow inner lines, except in snowy regions.

differs.how: Australia has no yellow inner lines, except snowy areas

nz-XoPE.title: Pole: small white horizontal sticker
nz-XoPE.summary: A small white horizontal sticker with several numbers, found in parts of the North Island. The plate edges must be straight; rounded plates appear everywhere.

nz-YUUn.title: Plants: flax in long neat rows
nz-YUUn.summary: Flax grows across the country, but in long neat rows think of the far south.

nz-Yk95.title: Plants: low volcanic vegetation, cloudy peaks
nz-Yk95.summary: Low volcanic plants around a national park with volcanoes whose tops are often in cloud.

nz-Z6C1.title: Pole: small black horizontal sticker
nz-Z6C1.summary: A small black horizontal sticker with several numbers, often in Taranaki and Wellington, rarely in nearby regions.

nz-ZfLj.title: Plants: dense red beech forest, snowy mountains
nz-ZfLj.summary: State Highway 94 has dense red beech forest surrounded by snow-capped mountains.

nz-ZjW9.title: Fence: long wooden post extensions
nz-ZjW9.summary: Much longer wooden extensions on fence posts, mainly in the far south and Hawke's Bay, sometimes Otago.

nz-aemR.title: Road lines: solid outer white lines, no middle
nz-aemR.summary: Solid outer white lines with no middle line are most common on the east cape, but also in northern Hawke's Bay and Wellington, where roads are narrower.

nz-dIFU.title: Pole: yellow triangle sticker, white boxes
nz-dIFU.summary: A warning sticker with a yellow danger triangle between two white rectangles, found in Hawke's Bay, between Lake Taupo and Lake Rotorua, northern Waikato and south of the biggest city.

nz-dqVU.title: Farming: vineyards
nz-dqVU.summary: Vineyards are especially common in one northern South Island region and one east coast North Island region, but can appear anywhere.

nz-eYDd.title: Pole: middle insulator on a tall metal bar
nz-eYDd.summary: The middle insulator sits on top of a tall metal bar, often on the border of the biggest city's region and the next one south, and elsewhere in that region. Shorter bars are rarer and appear everywhere.

nz-eaHz.title: Fence: thin metal posts
nz-eaHz.summary: Fences with thin metal posts are almost only on the South Island.

nz-f4UY.title: Plants: ferns in forests
nz-f4UY.summary: Ferns growing in forested areas are very common.

nz-fUk2.title: Phone numbers: 7 digits plus 2-digit area code
nz-fUk2.summary: Numbers are seven digits with a two-digit area code in front. Numbers starting with 02 are mobiles.

nz-hXrt.title: Sign: blue street signs with white text
nz-hXrt.summary: Blue street signs with white text, especially in rural areas. Other colours exist but blue is by far the most common. Australia almost never has blue ones.

differs.how: Australia almost never has blue street signs

nz-jvPP.title: Pole: off-centre crossbars
nz-jvPP.summary: Off-centre crossbars appear in Otago, Marlborough, Wellington and Taranaki.

nz-lGFJ.title: Landscape: glacial valley with lake and river
nz-lGFJ.summary: State Highway 80 runs north-south up a glacial valley, with snow-capped mountains on the west and a river and lake on the east.

nz-ljyw.title: Landscape: dried river bed with lots of gravel
nz-ljyw.summary: State Highway 73 near a mountain pass runs by an almost dry river with lots of gravel.

nz-lm-2256.title: Pole: black sticker, 7 digits, starts 1 or 4
nz-lm-2256.summary: Black vertical sticker with 7 digits starting with 1 or 4, rarely 3, found only in the western central North Island.

nz-lm-2257.title: Pole: code with P and 5 digits
nz-lm-2257.summary: An area in south-eastern Manawatū has pole codes starting with P followed by 5 digits.

nz-lm-2258.title: Pole: small red, white and blue dot stickers
nz-lm-2258.summary: At the far north-east tip, small pole stickers in red, white and blue (not always all three), round or rectangular.

nz-lm-2259.title: Pole: white sticker, 6 digits starting 30 or 31
nz-lm-2259.summary: A white-background sticker (black on white) with 6 digits plus a tag, starting with 30 or 31, means the biggest city or Northland.

nz-lm-2260.title: Pole: black sticker, 6-7 digits, starts 9
nz-lm-2260.summary: A black vertical code with six or seven digits, with or without a tag, starting with 9, means the biggest city or further north.

nz-lm-2261.title: Pole: small sticker, 2 letters and numbers
nz-lm-2261.summary: Between the two rivers around the biggest South Island city, 5-character codes start with two letters and are a bit smaller than other vertical black codes.

nz-lm-2262.title: Pole: sticker, 6 digits plus tag, starts with 2
nz-lm-2262.summary: Six digits plus a tag starting with 2 appears only on the very northern tip.

nz-mDBz.title: Landscape: bright sandy cliffs
nz-mDBz.summary: Bright sandy cliffs are common in the central-west North Island, and appear in parts of nearby regions and on one road into the east coast. They can look like sandy rocks.

nz-msuk.title: Bollard: black stripe instead of red
nz-msuk.summary: A normal bollard with a black stripe instead of red, common around the capital, especially in older Gen 3 coverage.

nz-nmR0.title: Farming: fruit farms under green netting
nz-nmR0.summary: Fruit farms covered in green netting, most common near one North Island port city and near the east-cape city. Not exclusive.

nz-oCAJ.title: Sign: give-way with white border, red text
nz-oCAJ.summary: Give-way signs have a white border and red text. Australia's use black text.

differs.how: Australian give-way signs use black text

nz-pIF3.title: Pole: yellow cow-tag-like tag
nz-pIF3.summary: A yellow tag like a cow tag is on most poles in the east-cape region, a few spots on the South Island, and northern Hawke's Bay.

nz-qFdG.title: Landscape: hill ranges north and south of a town
nz-qFdG.summary: A northern South Island town has a large range of hills to its north and to its south.

nz-qFtc.title: Pole: long square olive-brown possum guard
nz-qFtc.summary: Most poles in one northern South Island region have a long, square, olive-brown possum guard, alongside the usual shorter silver ones.

nz-rFlV.title: Pole: medium black vertical sticker, 5 digits
nz-rFlV.summary: A medium-sized black vertical sticker with 5 digits, found on the West Coast, Tasman, southern Canterbury and southern Northland.

nz-rGvH.title: Coverage: light snow on a southern highway
nz-rGvH.summary: Part of State Highway 85 in Otago has light snow, between Becks and Morrison.

nz-uxAD.title: Bollard: red band wrapping around the top
nz-uxAD.summary: A red band wraps around the top of the post, all the way round the back and part of the front. Front or back often has a thin yellow or white reflector. Unique to this country.

nz-xku9.title: Sign: yellow diamond warnings on white posts
nz-xku9.summary: Most direction and warning signs sit on white posts. Warning signs are yellow diamonds.

nz-ynPy.title: Landscape: smooth volcano, pointed top
nz-ynPy.summary: A volcano with smooth slopes and a pointed, often snowy peak, visible from afar because the area around it is flat.
